papers.title: GeoEPred: A multimodal structure-aware geometric deep learning framework for Gram-negative bacterial secreted effector prediction with sequence semantics.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of effector proteins secreted by Gram-negative bacteria is important for elucidating bacterial pathogenic mechanisms and developing precise anti-infective strategies. Although existing methods have benefited from the strong sequence feature extraction capacity of pretrained protein language models, reliance on linear sequence information alone often fails to fully capture the three-dimensional conformational signals required for virulence functions. Meanwhile, conventional structure-based methods are limited by the scarcity of experimentally resolved protein structures. To
papers.summary: GeoEPred is a multimodal deep learning framework that combines protein language model sequence embeddings with predicted 3D structural features to identify effector proteins secreted by Gram-negative bacteria. By integrating geometric deep learning on structures with sequence semantics, it aims to overcome the limitations of sequence-only and structure-only approaches, improving effector prediction for understanding bacterial pathogenesis.

papers.title: Rarefaction is better than robust Aitchison PCA and other compositional data analysis methods at controlling for uneven sequencing effort.
papers.abstract: Amplicon sequencing typically results in a wide distribution in the number of sequences obtained from each sample. How best to account for this variation has been a persistent problem in the microbial ecology literature. Historically, rarefaction has been used in ecology and this practice was adopted by microbial ecologists. However, rarefaction has been strongly criticized, leading to the development of compositional data analysis and normalization methods. Therefore, I reassessed the benchmarking data that were generated by the developers of one such method, robust Aitchison PCA. I found num
papers.summary: This study reanalyzes benchmarking data used to promote robust Aitchison PCA (RPCA) and finds that simple rarefaction actually controls for uneven sequencing depth better than RPCA and other compositional data analysis methods. The author argues that the field's move away from rarefaction may have been premature, at least for the goal of handling variable sequencing effort in amplicon data.

papers.title: stFormer integrates spatial ligand signaling into a foundation model for spatial transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Recent foundation models for single-cell transcriptomic data generate informative, context-aware gene and cell representations. Spatial transcriptomic (ST) data offer extra positional insights but were not considered by these single-cell models. We introduce stFormer, a transformer model tailored for ST data, which employs the cross-attention module to incorporate spatial ligand genes. To unify different ST technologies with a trade-off between resolution and gene coverage, we propose a biased cross-attention method that enables the model to do learning with single-cell resolution on whole-tra
papers.summary: stFormer is a transformer-based foundation model designed specifically for spatial transcriptomics data, using cross-attention to incorporate spatial ligand signaling genes into learned gene and cell representations. It introduces a biased cross-attention mechanism to unify diverse spatial transcriptomics platforms that differ in resolution and gene coverage, enabling single-cell-resolution learning on whole-transcriptome data.

papers.title: A Generalizable Multimodal Model for Treatment-Stratified Risk and Survival Assessment under Real-World Constraints: A Multi-Center Study of Colorectal Cancer.
papers.abstract: Integrating histopathology, genomic, and clinical phenotypes holds promise for improving prognostic patient stratification, including within treatment-defined subgroups, in colorectal cancer (CRC). However, ensuring the availability of all modalities in routine clinical practice remains challenging. Comprehensive molecular profiling is often constrained by cost and turnaround time, leaving histopathology as the most consistently available modality across institutions. In addition, variability in staining protocols, scanning devices, patient demographics, and outcome distributions across center
papers.summary: This multi-center study develops a generalizable multimodal model that integrates histopathology, genomic, and clinical data to stratify colorectal cancer patients by treatment and predict survival, while explicitly addressing real-world constraints where not all modalities are available. The model is designed to remain robust when only histopathology is accessible, accommodating variability in staining, scanning devices, and patient demographics across centers.

papers.title: AcrSeek: Metric Learning with Hybrid Negative Mining for Anti-CRISPR Protein Detection under Extreme Class Imbalance.
papers.abstract: Anti-CRISPR (Acr) proteins inhibit CRISPR-Cas immunity and are key targets for precise control of CRISPR-based genome editing and phage-host coevolution research. Their experimental identification is costly and low-throughput, so computational predictors are used to prioritise candidates for testing. In this setting validated positives number in the hundreds while phage-derived putative negatives reach tens of thousands, producing extreme class imbalance. Yet existing classification-based predictors train and evaluate on 1:1 balanced datasets and allow high-similarity sequences between trainin
papers.summary: AcrSeek is a new computational tool for detecting anti-CRISPR (Acr) proteins, which inhibit CRISPR-Cas immunity and are useful for controlling gene editing. Unlike prior predictors that train on artificially balanced datasets, AcrSeek uses metric learning with hybrid negative mining to handle the extreme class imbalance (hundreds of positives vs. tens of thousands of negatives) typical of real-world Acr discovery. This makes it better suited for prioritizing candidate Acr proteins for costly experimental validation.

papers.title: Post-Search Validation and Curation of Site-Resolved N‑Glycoproteomics Data.
papers.abstract: Given the significant role of glycosylation in modulating protein structure and activity, glycoproteomics is gaining increased interest from the broad scientific community. Large-scale site-resolved N-glycoproteomics relies on automated MS2-based searches, but candidate glycopeptide assignments can remain ambiguous when isomeric or isobaric glycan structures, adducts, chemical modifications, in-source fragments, or incomplete MS2 evidence support more than one plausible interpretation. Here, we systematically categorize common challenges and misassignments in glycoproteomics and present a post
papers.summary: This paper systematically catalogs common pitfalls and misassignments in automated MS2-based N-glycoproteomics searches, including ambiguities from isomeric/isobaric glycans, adducts, modifications, and incomplete MS2 evidence. It then presents a post-search validation and curation framework to improve confidence in site-resolved glycopeptide assignments.

papers.title: Enhanced Sampling of Protein Conformations in AlphaFold3 with Repulsive Bias in the Diffusion Generative Model.
papers.abstract: Conformational changes in proteins are vital to their function yet remain challenging for state-of-the-art artificial intelligence, such as AlphaFold3 (AF3), to predict. It has been observed that AF3 sometimes fails to capture ligand-induced conformational changes, even though it explicitly includes ligand molecules that induce such changes. To address this challenge, we develop an enhanced sampling scheme that leverages the diffusion-based generative model used in AF3 to predict protein structures. Interpreting the diffusion generative model as a stochastic sampling process analogous to molec
papers.summary: The authors introduce an enhanced sampling method that adds a repulsive bias to AlphaFold3's diffusion-based generative model to better capture alternative protein conformations, including ligand-induced conformational changes that AF3 often misses. By treating the diffusion process as a stochastic sampler analogous to molecular dynamics, they enable broader exploration of the conformational landscape. This improves AF3's ability to predict functionally relevant protein states.

papers.title: Development and validation of a multimodal MRI habitat-based deep learning fusion model for predicting 252Cf neutron therapy response in cervical cancer.
papers.abstract: Cervical cancer remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality among women worldwide. Although californium-252 (252Cf) neutron brachytherapy has demonstrated favorable therapeutic efficacy for locally advanced cervical cancer, substantial inter-patient heterogeneity in treatment response still exists. Therefore, developing a reliable non-invasive predictive model before treatment is of considerable clinical importance.
papers.summary: This study develops and validates a deep learning fusion model that combines multimodal MRI-based tumor 'habitat' imaging features to predict how cervical cancer patients will respond to californium-252 neutron brachytherapy. The goal is to provide a non-invasive, pre-treatment tool for anticipating treatment response amid substantial patient-to-patient heterogeneity.

papers.title: Lipid tail length dictates membrane disruption by carmofur analogs and reveals noncanonical modes of action.
papers.abstract: Carmofur, a lipidated urethane derivative and prodrug of 5-fluorouracil, has an established clinical application as an antineoplastic agent for the treatment of colorectal cancer, primarily through inhibition of acid ceramidase and subsequent intracellular drug release. Beyond this oncological application, recent drug repurposing efforts have identified covalent inhibition of the SARS-CoV-2 main protease as an additional antiviral mechanism. The pronounced amphiphilic character of carmofur, arising from a polar fluoropyrimidine headgroup appended to a hydrophobic aliphatic tail, raises the pos
papers.summary: This study investigates how the length of the lipid tail in carmofur analogs affects their ability to disrupt membranes, revealing that tail length is a key determinant of membrane activity. The findings suggest that carmofur and its analogs may act through noncanonical mechanisms beyond their known targets, such as acid ceramidase and the SARS-CoV-2 main protease. This work provides insight into the structure-activity relationships that govern membrane interactions of amphiphilic drugs.

papers.title: CheckAMG: Accurate Identification of Auxiliary Viral Genes with Genome-Language Models.
papers.abstract: Viruses shape microbial metabolism through auxiliary viral genes (AVGs) that reprogram host metabolism, physiology, and gene regulation during infection. Identifying AVGs is complicated by ambiguous viral versus cellular assignment, inconsistent curation, and reliance on sequence homology that misses divergent functions. Here we present CheckAMG, which pairs annotation-based AVG prediction, curated with a per-gene viral scoring system and ontological mapping of metabolic function, with a finetuned genome-language model for annotation-independent discovery. Benchmarked against DRAM-V and VIBRAN
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: CheckAMG is a new tool for identifying auxiliary viral genes (AVGs) that viruses use to reprogram host metabolism during infection. It combines annotation-based prediction with a curated viral scoring system and a fine-tuned genome-language model to detect divergent AVGs that homology-based methods miss, outperforming existing tools DRAM-V and VIBRANT in benchmarks.

papers.title: Transformer-Based Multitask Framework Integrating Habitat and Deep Learning for Predicting Early Disease Control and Survival in Immunotherapy-Treated Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients show heterogeneous responses to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). This study developed ECOS-Net, a transformer-based multitask network integrating CT-derived habitat and 2.5-dimensional (2.5D) deep learning features for simultaneously predicting early disease control (DC) and overall survival (OS). Of 1,234 patients with HCC enrolled from eight institutions and public databases, 832 ICI-treated patients were used for model development. ECOS-Net fused features using multi-head attention and generated early DC probabilities and OS risk scores. ECOS-DC a
papers.summary: This study introduces ECOS-Net, a transformer-based multitask deep learning framework that combines CT-derived habitat imaging features with 2.5D deep learning to simultaneously predict early disease control and overall survival in hepatocellular carcinoma patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors. Trained on 832 ICI-treated patients from eight institutions, the model aims to address heterogeneous treatment responses by fusing imaging features via multi-head attention.

papers.title: ASAS-NANP SYMPOSIUM: MATHEMATICAL MODELING IN ANIMAL NUTRITION: The Evolution of Large Language Models and Their Impact on Animal Sciences.
papers.abstract: The rapid rise of large language models (LLM) is reshaping the scientific landscape, transitioning from early statistical language models to advanced transformer-based architectures capable of synthesizing knowledge across disciplines. While their predictive capacity and scalability have opened new avenues in data analysis, hypothesis generation, and decision support, concerns remain regarding bias, hallucination, reproducibility, and ethical governance. In animal sciences, LLM are gradually applied to challenges in nutrition modeling, animal health, genetic selection, and sustainability. Prec
papers.summary: This symposium paper reviews the evolution of large language models from early statistical approaches to modern transformer architectures and discusses their emerging applications in animal sciences, including nutrition modeling, animal health, genetic selection, and sustainability. It also highlights key concerns such as bias, hallucination, reproducibility, and ethical governance that must be addressed for responsible adoption.

papers.title: Agentic campaign control for high-throughput de novo binder design.
papers.abstract: Progress in artificial intelligence has produced a rapidly growing ecosystem of methods for de novo protein design. With access to many specialized and often complementary tools, how does one use them effectively, especially with a finite compute budget? Here, we introduce Target-adaptive Rescue-Explore-eXploit (T-REX) , an agentic protein binder design framework that orchestrates multiple state-of-the-art protein generative models and structure evaluators. Over the course of a design campaign, T-REX leverages large language model (LLM) agents to reason over accumulating outcomes and decide wh
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: T-REX is an agentic framework that uses LLM agents to orchestrate multiple protein generative models and structure evaluators for de novo binder design. It adaptively decides which tools to use as results accumulate, aiming to make design campaigns more effective under finite compute budgets.

papers.title: CardioChrom Reconstructs the Human Cardiac Virtual Epigenome from Single-Nucleus Transcriptomes.
papers.abstract: Matched epigenomic profiling remains scarce in human heart failure, limiting regulatory interpretation of single-nucleus ribonucleic acid (RNA) sequencing data. We developed CardioChrom, a cardiac-specialized framework that reconstructs chromatin accessibility, histone H3 lysine 27 acetylation (H3K27ac), and histone H3 lysine 27 trimethylation (H3K27me3) from single-nucleus RNA profiles.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: CardioChrom is a cardiac-specialized computational framework that predicts three epigenomic marks (chromatin accessibility, H3K27ac, and H3K27me3) directly from single-nucleus RNA sequencing profiles of human heart tissue. This enables regulatory interpretation of snRNA-seq data in heart failure studies where matched epigenomic profiling is scarce.

papers.title: DesignMaster: A Multi-Conditional Diffusion Framework for Rational PROTAC Design.
papers.abstract: Proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) enable targeted protein degradation through ternary complex formation with E3 ubiquitin ligase. However, the rational design of PROTACs remains highly challenging due to limited structure-activity relationship data and the vast conformational diversity of linkers. Existing computational approaches can be broadly divided into structure-based ternary modelling methods and fragment-based linker generation models. Although these approaches have advanced PROTAC design, they typically neglect key physicochemical constraints and linker-length control during th
papers.summary: DesignMaster introduces a multi-conditional diffusion framework for the rational design of PROTAC molecules, which are drugs that degrade target proteins by recruiting E3 ubiquitin ligases. Unlike prior structure-based or fragment-based methods, it incorporates physicochemical constraints and linker-length control during generation, addressing a key gap in computational PROTAC design.

papers.title: A SHAP-Based Interpretable Model for MDRO-Infection Risk in Chronically Multimorbid Middle-Aged and Elderly ICU Adults.
papers.abstract: Multidrug-resistant organism (MDRO) infection poses a significant clinical challenge, resulting in poor outcomes for middle-aged and older intensive care unit (ICU) patients with chronic multimorbidity. While conventional prediction models can identify high-risk patients, they often lack transparency in clinical decision-making. To bridge this gap, we aimed to develop a prediction model that incorporates Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP)-based explainability analysis. This approach aims to achieve accurate risk prediction while quantitatively assessing the contribution of each risk factor,
papers.journal: British journal of hospital medicine (London, England : 2005)
papers.summary: This study develops a machine learning model to predict multidrug-resistant organism (MDRO) infection risk in middle-aged and elderly ICU patients with chronic multimorbidity, using SHAP (Shapley Additive Explanations) to make the model's predictions interpretable. The approach aims to identify high-risk patients while quantifying how much each clinical risk factor contributes to the prediction, supporting more transparent clinical decision-making.

papers.title: Multi-Granular Embedding and Hybrid Encoder-Decoder Architecture with Temporal Linear Regression Bypass for Sensor-Based Time Series Forecasting in Smart Infrastructure.
papers.abstract: In this work, we propose a robust deep encoder-decoder neural network that integrates multiple deep sequence models for time series forecasting in sensor-based applications. The proposed approach features a sophisticated input embedding layer that integrates scalar features, position encodings, and multi-granularity time embeddings. To improve computational efficiency, we employ a generative-style decoder inspired by the Informer architecture, which enables full-length sequence prediction in a single iteration, avoiding the latency associated with traditional autoregressive models. The archite
papers.summary: The authors propose a deep encoder-decoder neural network for forecasting sensor-based time series in smart infrastructure, combining multiple sequence models with a rich input embedding layer that fuses scalar features, positional encodings, and multi-granularity time embeddings. A generative-style decoder inspired by Informer enables full-length sequence prediction in a single pass, and a temporal linear regression bypass is added to improve accuracy and efficiency.

papers.title: Proteomic Signatures of Cardiac Mitochondrial Remodelling During Acute Diabetes Reflect Metabolic and Redox Adaptations.
papers.abstract: Mitochondria play a central role in cardiac energy metabolism and dynamically adapt to changes in metabolic demand. However, the early mitochondrial adaptations accompanying the acute phase of diabetes mellitus remain insufficiently understood. This study aimed to characterise diabetes-induced mitochondrial remodelling in the rat heart.
papers.summary: This study uses proteomics to characterize how cardiac mitochondria remodel during the acute phase of diabetes in a rat model. The findings reveal changes in metabolic and redox-related protein signatures, suggesting early mitochondrial adaptations to the diabetic environment.

papers.title: Combined Analysis of Transcriptome and Metabolome of Large-Size Triploid Rainbow Trout in Different Seasons.
papers.abstract: Seasonal temperature variation poses a significant physiological challenge for cold-water aquaculture species; however, the molecular mechanisms underlying seasonal adaptation in large-sized triploid rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss) remain largely unexplored. In this study, we integrated liver transcriptomics and LC-MS-based untargeted metabolomics across four seasons (February, May, August, November) to investigate this phenomenon. Seasonal comparisons revealed pronounced molecular reprogramming, with the comparison between May and August showing the largest transcriptomic shift (13,359 di
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.summary: This study integrated liver transcriptomics and untargeted metabolomics in large triploid rainbow trout across four seasons to uncover molecular mechanisms of seasonal temperature adaptation. The largest transcriptomic shift occurred between May and August, revealing pronounced seasonal molecular reprogramming in this cold-water aquaculture species.

papers.title: ConFormer-Net: Spatiotemporal Modeling for Landslide Detection Using Multi-Temporal SAR Data.
papers.abstract: Landslides are characterized by sudden occurrence, severe destructiveness, and widespread spatial distribution. Therefore, rapid and accurate landslide detection is essential for reducing infrastructure damage and safeguarding human lives. Conventional landslide monitoring methods are generally time-consuming, labor-intensive, and inefficient, while existing deep learning-based landslide detection methods remain limited in multiscale spatial structure representation, temporal sequence modeling, and spatiotemporal feature fusion. To address these limitations, this study proposes ConFormer-Net,
papers.summary: ConFormer-Net is a deep learning architecture that combines convolutional neural networks with transformer components to detect landslides from multi-temporal synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery. The model is designed to better capture multiscale spatial structures, temporal sequences, and fused spatiotemporal features than prior deep learning approaches. It aims to enable faster, more accurate landslide detection for disaster response and infrastructure protection.

papers.title: Beyond Accuracy: A Reliability-Oriented Multi-Dimensional Benchmark of Data-Driven Fault Diagnosis for Liquid Rocket Engines.
papers.abstract: Liquid rocket engines (LREs) are mission-critical propulsion systems whose reliability directly affects launch safety and the repeated operation of reusable launch vehicles. Data-driven LRE fault diagnosis remains difficult because labeled fault samples are scarce, engine-to-engine variations cause distribution shifts, and existing evaluations frequently emphasize classification accuracy without controlling for input representation. This study establishes a reliability-oriented benchmark that evaluates seven representative machine-learning and deep-learning methods from four dimensions: diagno
papers.summary: This paper introduces a reliability-oriented benchmark for data-driven fault diagnosis in liquid rocket engines, evaluating seven machine learning and deep learning methods across four dimensions beyond simple classification accuracy. It addresses key challenges like scarce labeled fault samples, engine-to-engine distribution shifts, and inconsistent input representations, aiming to provide a more realistic assessment of diagnostic reliability.

papers.title: A reference genome without a virus: cDNA reconstruction reveals the provenance and function of the MS2 phage sequence.
papers.abstract: Reference genomes are often treated as faithful representations of experimentally validated viral genomes, yet the relationship between historically curated reference sequences and infectivity is rarely tested experimentally. Here, we developed a cDNA-based reconstruction platform for the canonical RNA phage MS2 and used it to compare the current NCBI reference genome (RefSeq) with closely related published isolate sequences. We found that isolate-derived sequences reproducibly yielded infectious phage, whereas the current MS2 RefSeq-derived construct did not, showing that the present referenc
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors built a cDNA-based reverse genetics platform for the RNA phage MS2 and found that the current NCBI RefSeq reference genome does not produce infectious phage, while closely related published isolate sequences do. This shows that the curated reference sequence has accumulated errors or artifacts that break infectivity, and that isolate-derived sequences better reflect the true biological virus.

papers.title: Mapping Gene Expression to an Interpretable Semantic Space.
papers.abstract: Cell embeddings organize single-cell expression data, but their dimensions have no biological meaning, so clusters are interpreted afterward. We present MESIC (Mapping Expression to Semantic space with Interpretable Components), which builds the written knowledge about genes held in curated databases into the dimensions themselves. A biomedical language model converts each gene's summary into a semantic embedding. MESIC compresses these embeddings into a small number of components, each concentrated on a small set of genes and explained by their annotations. The components are computed once fr
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: MESIC is a new method that builds single-cell embeddings whose dimensions are directly interpretable by mapping each gene's curated database description into a semantic space using a biomedical language model. The resulting components are concentrated on small gene sets and can be explained by their annotations, eliminating the need for post-hoc cluster interpretation. This allows biological meaning to be read directly from embedding dimensions.

papers.title: HERA: Bioinspired Separation of Local Fault Response and Language-Model Scheduling in Simulated Quadruped Control.
papers.abstract: Language-model inference can delay emergency supervision, but cancellation alone cannot provide an immediate physical response. HERA (Hierarchical Event-driven Reflex Architecture) separates a measurement-driven deterministic local action from language-service scheduling, with biological inspiration limited to temporal separation and local feedback. A fixed 1472-trial campaign evaluated canonical-command scheduling, simulated actuator faults and live integration. Across three workloads, the mean validated-command latency was 0.486-0.512 s with preemption, 1.476-11.101 s with single-lane FIFO a
papers.summary: HERA is a control architecture for simulated quadruped robots that separates fast, deterministic local reflex responses from slower language-model-based scheduling. A 1472-trial campaign showed that preemptive scheduling reduced validated-command latency to roughly 0.5 seconds versus 1.5-11 seconds with single-lane FIFO, while still allowing language-model supervision. The work suggests that temporal separation of local feedback and language services can improve emergency responsiveness in robot control.

papers.title: 3D Spatial Interactomics Maps the Dynamics of NF-κB Multiprotein Signalosomes in Single Cells.
papers.abstract: NFκB signaling drives inflammatory responses by rapidly assembling membrane-proximal multiprotein supercomplexes, yet how these assemblies are organized in space and time within the 3D interior of a single cell has remained uncharacterized. We addressed this by profiling endogenous NFκB protein-protein interactions with an intelligent sequential proximity ligation assay (iseqPLA), read out by spinning disk confocal microscopy and 3D reconstruction. Each detected protein-protein proximity event is represented by a rolling-circle amplification product, and we treat clusters of co-localized punct
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint introduces iseqPLA, a sequential proximity ligation assay combined with spinning-disk confocal microscopy and 3D reconstruction, to map endogenous NF-κB protein-protein interactions in single cells. The method visualizes how membrane-proximal multiprotein signalosomes assemble and change over space and time within the 3D cell interior. It provides a new way to study dynamic signaling complexes at single-cell resolution.

papers.title: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Cell Types in Describing Neuronal Physiological Features.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) captures detailed gene expression profiles at scale, while patch-clamp recordings measure intrinsic neuronal electrophysiological properties. Modeling the relations between these two modalities remains a challenge. Here, we compare how well electrophysiological features can be predicted by traditional transcriptomic cell type classification, representations derived from a foundational model (scGPT) pretrained on large-scale scRNA-seq datasets, ion channel-coding genes, and highly variable genes. Using paired transcriptomic and electrophysiological patch-s
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study compares how well different transcriptomic representations predict neuronal electrophysiological features from paired patch-clamp and scRNA-seq data. Traditional cell type classifications perform surprisingly well, rivaling or exceeding more complex representations like scGPT embeddings, ion channel genes, and highly variable genes. The findings suggest that discrete cell type labels remain a powerful and simple way to link gene expression to neuronal physiology.

papers.title: Protein eXplosion Imaging (PXI): Protein Structures from Laser-Driven Explosions.
papers.abstract: We investigate the structural information retained in the distribution of explosion ion trajectories from proteins subjected to strong ionization. Using molecular-dynamics simulations and machine-learning analysis benchmarked against an analytical approach, we show that low-resolution structural information can be retrieved from the explosion distributions alone. An ensemble of convolutional neural networks trained on simulated spherical ion maps recovers the radius of gyration and the three semi-axes of an ellipsoidal molecular envelope with prediction errors of 1.2 Å and 1.5 Å, respectively,
papers.summary: This paper explores whether structural information about proteins can be recovered from the ion trajectories produced when proteins are exploded by intense laser ionization. Using molecular dynamics simulations and convolutional neural networks trained on simulated spherical ion maps, the authors recover the radius of gyration and the three semi-axes of an ellipsoidal molecular envelope with errors of 1.2 Å and 1.5 Å, respectively. The work suggests a proof-of-concept route to low-resolution protein shape determination from explosion imaging data.

papers.title: Quality-Aware AIoT-Enabled Wireless Urban Sensor Networks Using Deep Learning.
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the relationship between data quality and deep learning model performance for predicting pedestrian flows in smart cities, using data from the UK's Newcastle Urban Observatory. We evaluate eight forecasting models (including multivariate LSTMs and Transformers) across 110 pedestrian sensors. Crucially, by preserving genuine data gaps, we reveal that the structure of missing data-specifically the length of consecutive sequences-is a more significant determinant of model performance than overall data completeness. Segmented regression identifies a sharp breakpoint at thre
papers.summary: This paper analyzes how the structure of missing data affects deep learning forecasting of pedestrian flows across 110 urban sensors in Newcastle. It finds that the length of consecutive data gaps matters more for model performance than overall data completeness, with a sharp breakpoint identified at three consecutive missing values. The work suggests data quality assessment should focus on gap structure rather than simple completeness metrics.

papers.title: miRAssist: a context-aware, evidence integration framework for interpretable miRNA-target prioritization.
papers.abstract: MicroRNA-target interaction prediction remains challenging because many existing tools provide prediction scores or ranked candidate lists without making the supporting evidence easy to interpret or relate to a specific biological context.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: miRAssist is a new computational framework that predicts microRNA-target interactions by integrating multiple sources of evidence in a context-aware manner. Unlike existing tools that output opaque scores or ranked lists, it aims to make the underlying evidence interpretable and tied to specific biological contexts. This could help researchers prioritize miRNA-target pairs more reliably and understand why a given interaction is predicted.

papers.title: Self-supervised plasma proteomic representations for prospective disease prediction across varying protein availability.
papers.abstract: Large-scale plasma proteomics offers opportunities to characterize disease susceptibility and improve prospective risk prediction, but transferring proteomic predictors across datasets remains challenging because measured protein sets differ across cohorts, study phases and assay configurations. Here we developed a self-supervised protein-token Transformer that maps the proteins observed in each sample to a fixed-dimensional participant representation, allowing unavailable proteins to be omitted rather than imputed. Using plasma proteomic profiles from 53,014 participants in the UK Biobank Pha
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: The authors developed a self-supervised Transformer model that converts plasma proteomic profiles into fixed-dimensional participant representations while naturally handling missing proteins by omission rather than imputation. Applied to 53,014 UK Biobank participants, the approach enables prospective disease risk prediction that transfers across cohorts with differing protein panels. This addresses a key barrier to deploying proteomic predictors in heterogeneous real-world datasets.

papers.title: Predicting Capsid Protein Binding Sites in Single-Stranded RNA Viruses Using Machine Learning from Local Geometric Features.
papers.abstract: Selective recognition of viral RNA by capsid proteins is essential for genome packaging during the assembly of single-stranded RNA (ssRNA) viruses. However, identification of capsid protein binding sites in the RNA genome remains challenging because current experimental techniques are labor-intensive and low-throughput, motivating the development of computational approaches. Here, we present a sequence-based framework that integrates RNA tertiary structural modeling, local geometric feature extraction, and machine learning to predict capsid protein binding sites. Using the Qβ bacteriophage as
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors developed a computational framework that combines RNA tertiary structure modeling, local geometric feature extraction, and machine learning to predict where capsid proteins bind on single-stranded RNA viral genomes. Using the Qβ bacteriophage as a test case, they aim to overcome the labor-intensive and low-throughput nature of experimental binding site identification. This offers a sequence-based approach for studying viral genome packaging.

papers.title: Predicting Supramolecular Self-Assembly of Peptide Structures with AlphaFold3.
papers.abstract: Self-assembled peptide-based nanostructures have diverse applications in the pharmaceutical and materials fields, but accurately predicting their self-assembly behavior without time-intensive organic synthesis and characterization remains a significant challenge. Here, we assess the effectiveness of AlphaFold3 (AF3), a deep learning model for protein structure prediction, in modeling peptide-based nanostructures and the interactions driving supramolecular self-assembly. We designed amphiphilic peptides composed of alternating hydrophobic residues (valine, leucine, isoleucine, phenylalanine) an
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint evaluates whether AlphaFold3, a deep learning protein structure prediction model, can accurately model peptide-based supramolecular self-assemblies. Using designed amphiphilic peptides with alternating hydrophobic residues, the authors test AF3's ability to predict the interactions driving self-assembly without requiring synthesis and characterization. The work explores extending AF3 beyond single-protein folding to supramolecular nanostructure prediction.

papers.title: dictyBase 2026: a reimplementation of the Dictyostelium model organism database on minimal infrastructure.
papers.abstract: Dictyostelium discoideum is a model organism used to investigate a wide array of biological processes including chemotaxis, cell motility, phagocytosis, multicellular development, and autophagy. Many of its genes have human orthologs implicated in disease, making it a useful model organism for studying conditions ranging from cancer to neurodegeneration. dictyBase has served this community for two decades as a home for genomic data, protocols, a stock center, and community news. Here we describe a complete reimplementation of dictyBase as a self-contained service that uses static data files ra
papers.summary: dictyBase, the long-standing model organism database for Dictyostelium discoideum, has been completely reimplemented as a self-contained service built on static data files and minimal infrastructure. This redesign aims to reduce maintenance burden while continuing to provide genomic data, protocols, stock center information, and community resources for the Dictyostelium research community.

papers.title: Comparative Study of Anatomical and Learned Features in AI Models for Structural Brain MRI.
papers.abstract: In this work, we comprehensively evaluate three popular feature-extractionparadigms in AI-based neuroimaging modeling: (1) computation of anatomicalsurfaces and volumes, (2) supervised learning with convolutional neural net-works (CNNs), and (3) unsupervised pretraining of vision transformer (ViT)foundation models, followed by supervised finetuning. Our study is based on18 publicly available datasets containing 3D structural T1-weighted MRI scansfrom approximately 80,000 participants across seven distinct clinical tasks. Weobserve that a linear model based on anatomical features matches the di
papers.summary: This study compares three feature-extraction approaches for AI models on structural brain MRI: traditional anatomical surface/volume measurements, supervised CNNs, and unsupervised pretrained ViT foundation models with finetuning. Using 18 public datasets (~80,000 participants, seven clinical tasks), the authors find that a simple linear model built on anatomical features performs comparably to the deep learning approaches.

papers.title: A Transferable Genomic Language Model Framework for Fungal Gene Essentiality Prediction.
papers.abstract: Predicting biological function from genomic sequence remains a major challenge in computational and systems biology. Here, we tested whether the genomic language model Evo2, which encodes context-dependent DNA sequence patterns into embeddings, enables prediction of essential genes in fungi, a phenotype central to fungal biology and antifungal target discovery. We found that model performance was constrained not by the type or complexity of the downstream classifier, but by the biological information contained in Evo2 DNA embeddings. Specifically, the information recoverable from these embeddi
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint tests whether the genomic language model Evo2 can predict essential genes in fungi using DNA sequence embeddings. The authors find that prediction performance is limited primarily by the biological information encoded in the Evo2 embeddings rather than by the choice of downstream classifier, suggesting current genomic language models capture only partial functional signal for this task.

papers.title: Fast structural search for classification of gut bacterial mucin O-glycan degrading enzymes.
papers.abstract: The Enzyme Commission (EC) numbering scheme provides a hierarchical way to classify enzymes according to their catalytic functions. While recent protein language model (PLM) based approaches like CLEAN and ProteInter have improved sequence-based EC number prediction, they struggle with fine-grained classification at the deepest hierarchical level. Structure-based approaches for grouping similar proteins using alignment tools excel at finding proteins that share overall global structure, but suffer from high false positive rates when classifying proteins that are globally structurally similar b
papers.summary: The authors present a fast structural search method for classifying gut bacterial enzymes that degrade mucin O-glycans, addressing the difficulty of fine-grained EC number prediction at the deepest hierarchical level. Their approach improves on sequence-based protein language model methods (CLEAN, ProteInter) and global structural alignment tools, which suffer from high false positive rates when proteins are globally similar but functionally distinct.

papers.title: Multiscale cross modal fusion and cascaded signal propagation for drug target interaction prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of drug-target interaction (DTI) facilitates the translation of lead compounds into clinical therapeutics. Despite progress in deep learning, two challenges remain: the representation gap between heterogeneous drug and protein modalities and insufficient use of complementary knowledge from pretrained encoders. To address these issues, we propose SF-DTI, a unified framework that integrates multi-encoder protein fusion, structure-semantic drug alignment, and progressive cross-modal refinement for DTI prediction. Specifically, SF-DTI captures global protein semantics from mult
papers.summary: The paper introduces SF-DTI, a deep learning framework for predicting drug-target interactions that combines multi-encoder protein fusion, structure-semantic drug alignment, and progressive cross-modal refinement. It aims to bridge the representation gap between heterogeneous drug and protein modalities and better exploit complementary knowledge from pretrained encoders. The approach is evaluated on DTI prediction benchmarks, though the abstract is truncated before results are described.

papers.title: pLM-HP: Peptide hormone prediction using pre-trained protein language model representations.
papers.abstract: Peptide hormones play key roles in metabolic regulation, growth and development, and the maintenance of homeostasis and are important targets for drug discovery and design. However, traditional experimental methods for screening and identifying peptide hormones are costly and inefficient. Although existing machine learning methods have made some progress, they pay limited attention to class imbalance, and there is still room to improve prediction performance.
papers.summary: pLM-HP is a machine-learning method that uses representations from a pre-trained protein language model to predict peptide hormones, explicitly addressing class imbalance to improve performance over prior approaches. It aims to make peptide hormone screening faster and cheaper than experimental methods, supporting drug discovery and design.

papers.title: Progressive remodeling of global protein interaction networks in a mouse model of tauopathy.
papers.abstract: Neurodegenerative disease is marked not just by loss of proteins or cells, but by dynamic rewiring of macromolecular interaction networks that precede and drive pathology. Here, we present a temporally resolved, systems-scale map of multi-protein complex remodeling in a tauopathy model, integrating co-fractionation mass spectrometry, quantitative phosphoproteomics, and machine learning to decode phosphorylation-dependent shifts in protein interactomes across disease progression. This interactomic atlas serves as a resource to investigate functional assemblies, including MAPT-Dpysl2 and Cyfip1-
papers.summary: This study maps how protein interaction networks progressively rewire over the course of disease in a mouse model of tauopathy, using co-fractionation mass spectrometry, phosphoproteomics, and machine learning. The resulting interactomic atlas reveals phosphorylation-dependent shifts in multi-protein complexes and identifies specific assemblies such as MAPT-Dpysl2 and Cyfip1-containing complexes. It provides a temporal resource for understanding how network remodeling precedes and drives neurodegeneration.

papers.title: Beyond affinity: AI-supported developability assessment and multi-objective optimization in antibody development.
papers.abstract: Therapeutic antibodies are a major class of medicines, but high target affinity alone does not ensure manufacturability, stability, safety, or clinical success. Developability has therefore become a central constraint in antibody engineering and has pushed the field beyond affinity-first screening toward multi-objective decision-making. Machine-learning-based models increasingly integrate antibody sequence, structure, interaction, and assay data to estimate properties such as affinity, specificity, aggregation, viscosity, solubility, stability, immunogenicity, and pharmacokinetics before exper
papers.summary: This review argues that therapeutic antibody development must move beyond affinity-first screening to multi-objective optimization of developability properties such as stability, solubility, aggregation, viscosity, immunogenicity, and pharmacokinetics. It surveys how machine-learning models integrate sequence, structure, interaction, and assay data to predict these properties before experimental testing.

papers.title: A dual-tower multimodal framework with feature quality enhancement for predicting pathological complete response after neoadjuvant chemotherapy in breast cancer: a multicenter study.
papers.abstract: Pathological complete response (pCR) is a key endpoint following neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) in breast cancer, with potential to guide treatment adaptation and surgical de-escalation. However, limited generalizability across institutions remains a major challenge due to heterogeneous imaging protocols (scanner vendors, field strengths, and acquisition parameters) and diverse patient populations, which can cause significant domain shifts in model performance. This study develops and externally validates a multimodal framework for post-neoadjuvant, preoperative prediction of pCR using multipa
papers.summary: This study develops a dual-tower multimodal deep learning framework that predicts pathological complete response (pCR) after neoadjuvant chemotherapy in breast cancer by integrating multiparametric imaging with clinical data. The framework includes feature quality enhancement to address domain shifts caused by heterogeneous imaging protocols across institutions, and it is externally validated in a multicenter setting. The approach aims to improve generalizability of pCR prediction to support treatment adaptation and surgical de-escalation decisions.

papers.title: Network pharmacology, single-cell transcriptomics, machine learning and experimental validation identifying CHEK2 and HPGD as key therapeutic targets of berberine in diabetic nephropathy.
papers.abstract: Diabetic nephropathy (DN) is a severe microvascular complication of diabetes with limited therapeutic options. Berberine exhibits renoprotective potential, yet its precise molecular targets and mechanisms of action in DN remain unclear. Berberine targets were retrieved from TCMSP, SEA, and SwissTargetPrediction databases. Bulk transcriptomic microarray datasets (GSE96804, GSE30122) and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) dataset (GSE131882) were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO). Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) wer
papers.summary: This study integrates network pharmacology, bulk and single-cell transcriptomics, and machine learning to identify CHEK2 and HPGD as key targets through which berberine may protect against diabetic nephropathy. Experimental validation supports these targets, suggesting a multi-target mechanism for berberine's renoprotective effects.

papers.title: Gut microbiota signatures and machine learning-based candidate feature prioritization in advanced colorectal cancer.
papers.abstract: This single-center, cross-sectional case-control study aimed to characterize the gut microbiome profiles of patients with advanced colorectal cancer (CRC), identify candidate microbial features, and explore how well these features distinguished advanced CRC cases from healthy controls within the study dataset. Fecal samples were collected from 72 treatment-naïve patients with advanced CRC and 61 healthy controls. Microbial community structure was profiled using high-throughput sequencing of the V3-V4 region of the 16 S rRNA gene. The analytical pipeline included α/β-diversity analysis, multile
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study profiled the gut microbiome of 72 treatment-naïve advanced colorectal cancer patients and 61 healthy controls using 16S rRNA sequencing, finding distinct microbial community structures between groups. Machine learning was then used to prioritize candidate microbial features that best distinguished advanced CRC cases from controls within this dataset. The work highlights specific gut microbiota signatures as potential biomarkers, though findings are limited to a single-center cohort.

papers.title: Rethinking input complexity in transformer-based clinical prediction: implications for feature dimensionality and sequence length in longitudinal electronic health record data.
papers.abstract: Transformer-based models for clinical prediction using longitudinal electronic health record (EHR) data are often developed with large feature sets and long patient histories under the assumption that more data improves performance. However, high-dimensional inputs and long sequences increase computational burden, potentially limiting scalability. We evaluated how feature dimensionality and sequence length affect predictive performance, calibration, risk stratification, and computational efficiency in EHR prediction.
papers.summary: This study systematically tests the common assumption that transformer-based clinical prediction models benefit from ever-larger feature sets and longer patient histories in longitudinal EHR data. The authors find that increasing input complexity does not consistently improve predictive performance, calibration, or risk stratification, while substantially raising computational costs. Their results suggest that more parsimonious input designs may be preferable for scalable clinical deployment.

papers.title: Integrating Multimodal MRI Habitat and Transformer-Based Pathomics to Predict High-Risk Molecular Subtypes and Explore Biological Mechanisms in Adult Diffuse Gliomas.
papers.abstract: This study aims to achieve accurate prediction of high-risk molecular subtypes of gliomas through a cross-scale Combined model, matching the model's classification metrics with patient risk stratification and exploring the underlying biological mechanisms.
papers.summary: This study develops a cross-scale combined model that integrates multimodal MRI habitat imaging with transformer-based pathomics to predict high-risk molecular subtypes in adult diffuse gliomas. The model's classification performance is linked to patient risk stratification, and the authors explore the underlying biological mechanisms associated with the predicted subtypes.

papers.title: A Deep-Learning Based Biomarker of Systemic Cellular Senescence Burden to Predict Mortality and Health Outcomes.
papers.abstract: The accumulation of senescent cells is a recognized hallmark of biological aging and is associated with the onset of multiple chronic medical conditions. Senescent cells exhibit a distinct secretory profile, known as the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), which can propagate cellular senescence to neighboring and distant tissues. Measuring SASP factors in blood serves as a practical proxy for cellular senescence burden and may help track disease states and intervention outcomes. We developed and validated a composite SASP Score by integrating large-scale population proteomics da
papers.summary: The authors developed a composite SASP Score by integrating large-scale population proteomics data with deep learning to quantify systemic cellular senescence burden from blood biomarkers. This score was validated as a predictor of mortality and adverse health outcomes, offering a practical proxy for tracking senescence-related disease states and intervention effects.

papers.title: Combating antimicrobial resistance through multimodal data via artificial intelligence.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) poses a critical global health challenge, leading to substantial mortality and economic losses without science-based interventions. Conventional approaches to combating AMR have important limitations in addressing this escalating threat. Recent advances in AI, including deep learning, large language models, and protein language models, provide new opportunities to integrate multimodal data for AMR research. However, evidence remains uneven, with many approaches limited to computational benchmarking rather than real-world validation. Here, we critically review AI
papers.summary: This review examines how artificial intelligence, including deep learning, large language models, and protein language models, can integrate multimodal data to combat antimicrobial resistance. It highlights that while these approaches show promise, most evidence remains limited to computational benchmarking rather than real-world validation. The authors critically assess the current landscape and identify gaps for translating AI-driven AMR research into practice.

papers.title: Mechanism-aware and safety-validated AI for drug repurposing: a critical review and translational pharmacology framework.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted drug repurposing seeks to identify new therapeutic applications for existing drugs. Nevertheless, most of the existing studies are centered on prediction scores and candidate ranking, and there is still relatively little attention paid to the pharmacological mechanisms, safety and translational validation.
papers.summary: This critical review argues that AI-driven drug repurposing has focused too heavily on prediction scores and candidate ranking while neglecting pharmacological mechanism validation, safety assessment, and translational testing. The authors propose a translational pharmacology framework that integrates mechanism-awareness and safety validation into AI repurposing pipelines.

papers.title: From surveillance to intelligence: a scoping review of machine learning for antimicrobial resistance surveillance intelligence across One Health.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a leading global health threat requiring coordinated surveillance across human, animal, environmental, and genomic systems. Machine learning is increasingly applied to AMR data, yet its contribution to actionable surveillance intelligence, rather than prediction alone, remains poorly defined.
papers.summary: This scoping review examines how machine learning is being applied to antimicrobial resistance (AMR) surveillance data across human, animal, environmental, and genomic domains within a One Health framework. It argues that most current ML efforts focus on prediction rather than generating actionable surveillance intelligence, and identifies gaps in translating models into real-world decision support.

papers.title: Surveillance-Driven Machine Learning for Prediction of Antimicrobial Susceptibility: An Explainable Modeling Framework using the Pfizer ATLAS Dataset (2004 - 2023).
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a growing global public health threat, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where delayed antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) and limited diagnostic capacity complicate timely treatment and antimicrobial stewardship (AMS). Although large-scale surveillance programmes routinely collect antimicrobial susceptibility data, these datasets remain underutilised for predictive analytics.
papers.summary: This paper develops an explainable machine learning framework to predict antimicrobial susceptibility using 20 years of surveillance data from the Pfizer ATLAS dataset (2004–2023). The approach aims to support antimicrobial stewardship and treatment decisions, especially in low- and middle-income countries where rapid susceptibility testing is often unavailable. The study demonstrates how routinely collected surveillance data can be repurposed for predictive analytics.

papers.title: Structural and functional perspectives on DEAD-box RNA helicases in the rubber tree cold stress response.
papers.abstract: DExD/H-box RNA helicases constitute one of the largest families of adenosine triphosphate (ATP)-dependent nucleic-acid enzymes, with roles spanning the full breadth of RNA metabolism, from transcription to turnover. Their defining architectural feature is a conserved helicase core comprising two tandem RecA-like domains that couples ATP hydrolysis to duplex unwinding and ribonucleoprotein remodeling. Structural investigations have historically focused on human and yeast model systems, but recent methodological advances, particularly cryo-electron microscopy and deep learning-based structure pr
papers.summary: This review examines DEAD-box RNA helicases in the rubber tree (Hevea brasiliensis) and their roles in cold stress response, integrating structural insights from the conserved two-domain helicase core with functional data. It highlights how cryo-EM and deep learning-based structure prediction are expanding understanding of these enzymes beyond traditional human and yeast models to non-model plants.

papers.title: Integrative machine learning and transcriptomic analysis reveal a ferroptosis gene signature for pediatric Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia.
papers.abstract: Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia (MPP) is one of the most common causes of community-acquired pneumonia in children, affecting approximately 10%-40% of pediatric pneumonia cases worldwide. Despite advances in diagnostic and therapeutic approaches, the pathogenesis of severe MPP remains incompletely understood, and patients demonstrate highly heterogeneous responses to treatment. Recent evidence suggests that ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death, may play a critical role in the pathophysiology of MPP. This study aimed to elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying the in
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study integrates machine learning with transcriptomic data to identify a ferroptosis-related gene signature associated with pediatric Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia (MPP). The authors aim to clarify the molecular mechanisms underlying severe MPP and its heterogeneous treatment responses by linking ferroptosis pathways to disease pathogenesis. The work proposes a gene signature that could aid in understanding or stratifying pediatric MPP cases.

papers.title: Machine Learning in Stem Cell Research: From Biological Data to Clinical Translation.
papers.abstract: Stem cell (SC) research plays a central role in disease modeling and regenerative medicine, yet its clinical translation remains challenged by biological heterogeneity, incomplete cellular maturation, stringent quality-control requirements, and increasingly complex biological and clinical data. Machine learning (ML) has emerged as a powerful computational approach for extracting biologically meaningful information from these data, enabling quantitative characterization of SC behavior and predictive modeling across diverse experimental and translational applications. This review presents a unif
papers.summary: This review surveys how machine learning is being applied across stem cell research, from analyzing complex biological data to supporting clinical translation. It highlights how ML can address challenges like cellular heterogeneity, incomplete maturation, and quality control by enabling quantitative characterization and predictive modeling of stem cell behavior.

papers.title: Bio-Inspired Artificial Intelligence Multimorbidity Score for Human-Machine Clinical Risk Stratification.
papers.abstract: Multimorbidity is strongly associated with mortality, but existing comorbidity indices often generalize poorly across populations because they depend on fixed disease lists and context-specific weights. We developed the large-language-model-based multimorbidity score (LLM-MMS), a prompt-based large-language-model-derived multimorbidity phenotype score, as a bio-inspired artificial intelligence score for human-machine clinical risk stratification and evaluated it for all-cause mortality prediction in 770,439 adults from 9 international longitudinal cohorts. Harmonized participant-level data wer
papers.summary: The authors developed LLM-MMS, a prompt-based large language model-derived multimorbidity score, and evaluated it for predicting all-cause mortality in 770,439 adults across 9 international longitudinal cohorts. The score aims to overcome the poor generalizability of traditional fixed disease-list comorbidity indices by using a bio-inspired AI approach for human-machine clinical risk stratification.

papers.title: scLTF: A self-training clustering framework for large-scale single-cell RNA-Seq data.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) technology has rapidly advanced in recent years, driving significant breakthroughs in developmental biology, cancer research, immunology, and other related fields. However, existing clustering methods still face performance bottlenecks when handling large-scale scRNA-seq data. To address this challenge, we propose a self-training clustering method for large-scale single-cell RNA-seq data, termed scLTF (Single-cell Louvain-Transformer Framework for Large-scale Clustering). This method first generates preliminary clusters using a fast Louvain algorithm and
papers.summary: scLTF is a self-training clustering framework designed to handle large-scale scRNA-seq datasets, combining a fast Louvain algorithm for initial clustering with a Transformer-based refinement step. The approach aims to overcome performance bottlenecks of existing clustering methods when applied to very large single-cell datasets.
